parameters.jsonExample:
{
  "tenant_id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "conversation_id": "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222",
  "reason": "angry_customer",
  "priority": "high",
  "context_summary": "Customer is upset about a delayed refund and has asked twice for a human."
}

parameters.query:
select
  insert_escalation($1, $2, $3, $4, $5) as escalation_id,
  (select escalation_notify_email from ai_config where tenant_id = $1) as notify_email,
  (select name from tenants where id = $1) as tenant_name;

nodes.name: Insert Escalation
nodes.notes: notify_email and tenant_name pulled in the SAME query as the escalation insert -- one round trip, same lesson as everywhere else (a chained Postgres node here would replace $json with only insert_escalation's scalar return value and lose these).

nodes.name: Send Notification via Gmail
nodes.notes: Same known limitation as everywhere else in this codebase: one shared Gmail credential, not dynamic per-tenant. continueOnFail:true -- the escalation row is already saved by this point, so a notification failure never loses the escalation itself, only the push alert (it's still visible on the dashboard).
